title: Proverbs Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Proverbs 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A wise son heareth his father's instruction
The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing
The light of the righteous rejoiceth
questions.correctAnswer: A wise son heareth his father's instruction
questions.explanation: This appears in Proverbs 13:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:2, what will a man eat by the fruit of his mouth?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:2 states, 'A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth.'

questions.question: What does Proverbs 13:3 say a person who keeps his mouth keeps?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:3 says, 'He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life.'

questions.question: What happens to the soul of the sluggard according to Proverbs 13:4?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:4 states, 'The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:5, what kind of man hateth lying?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:5 says, 'A righteous man hateth lying.'

questions.question: What does righteousness do for the upright according to Proverbs 13:6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:6 states, 'Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way.'

questions.question: What is said about a man who maketh himself rich in Proverbs 13:7?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:7 says, 'There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:8, what are a man's riches called?
options: The ransom of a man's life
questions.correctAnswer: The ransom of a man's life
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:8 states, 'The ransom of a man's life are his riches.'

questions.question: What does the lamp of the wicked do according to Proverbs 13:9?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:9 says, 'The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.'

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:1, who heareth not rebuke?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:1 states, 'but a scorner heareth not rebuke.'

questions.question: What will the soul of transgressors eat according to Proverbs 13:2?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:2 says, 'but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence.'

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:4 says the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:4 states, 'but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.'

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:6 states that wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:6 says, 'but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.'

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13 says that the sluggard shall be made rich by his desires.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:4 states the soul of the sluggard desireth and hath nothing, so he is not made rich by his desires.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13 teaches that a righteous man is loathsome and cometh to shame.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:5 says a wicked man is loathsome and cometh to shame, not a righteous man.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:10, what is the cause of contention?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:10 states, 'Only by pride cometh contention,' identifying pride as the cause of contention.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 13:11 promise will happen if someone gathers wealth by labor as commanded in Proverbs 13:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:11 contrasts vain wealth with wealth gathered by labor, promising that laborious gathering leads to increase.

questions.question: What effect does 'hope deferred' have according to Proverbs 13:12?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:12 states, 'Hope deferred maketh the heart sick,' showing the emotional impact of delayed hope.

questions.question: What is the reward promised in Proverbs 13:13 for those who fear the commandment in Proverbs 13:12?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:13 says, 'he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded,' as a consequence of respecting God's word.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:14, what is described as 'a fountain of life'?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:14 calls 'The law of the wise' a fountain of life, emphasizing its life-giving wisdom.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 13:15 say is given by good understanding?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:15 states, 'Good understanding giveth favour,' highlighting the benefit of wisdom.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 13:16 describe the behavior of a prudent man compared to a fool?
options: He dealeth with knowledge; a fool layeth open his folly
He avoids labor; a fool gathers wealth
He fears the commandment; a fool despiseth the word
He is shamed; a fool is honoured
questions.correctAnswer: He dealeth with knowledge; a fool layeth open his folly
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:16 contrasts the prudent man's knowledge with the fool's exposed folly.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 13:17 associate with a wicked messenger?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:17 states, 'A wicked messenger falleth into mischief,' showing the danger of unfaithfulness.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:18, what comes to him who refuses instruction?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:18 warns that 'Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction,' linking disobedience to negative outcomes.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 13:13 say will happen to one who despiseth the word?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:13 clearly states that 'Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed,' emphasizing the seriousness of rejecting God's word.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 13:15 describe the way of transgressors?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:15 contrasts good understanding with the hard way of transgressors.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:11, what happens to wealth gotten by vanity?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:11 warns that 'Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished,' showing the unsustainability of ill-gotten gain.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:14 says the law of the wise helps to depart from the snares of death.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:14 describes 'The law of the wise' as 'a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.'

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:17 states that a faithful ambassador falls into mischief.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:17 contrasts a wicked messenger, who falls into mischief, with a faithful ambassador, who brings health.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:18 teaches that those who regard reproof shall be shamed.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:18 states that he who regards reproof shall be honoured, not shamed.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:19, what is described as 'sweet to the soul'?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:19 states 'The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul,' directly identifying the desire accomplished as sweet.

questions.question: In Proverbs 13:20, what is the consequence of walking with fools?
options: He shall eat to the satisfying of his soul
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:20 says 'a companion of fools shall be destroyed,' indicating destruction as the consequence.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 13:21 say pursues sinners?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:21 states 'Evil pursueth sinners,' making evil the pursuer of sinners.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 13:22, what does a good man leave to his children's children?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:22 clearly states 'A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children.'

questions.question: Proverbs 13:24 uses the metaphor of the rod to illustrate what parental attitude?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:24 says 'He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes,' linking love with timely discipline.

questions.question: What contrast does Proverbs 13:25 draw between the righteous and the wicked regarding sustenance?
options: The righteous eat to satisfaction, the wicked's belly shall want
The righteous sow for others, the wicked harvest for themselves
The righteous are poor, the wicked are rich
The righteous laugh, the wicked mourn
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous eat to satisfaction, the wicked's belly shall want
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:25 states 'The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want,' contrasting their nourishment.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chasteneth' (Proverbs 13:24) most accurately mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'chasteneth' (yuqach) in Proverbs 13:24 means to discipline or correct, emphasizing parental correction.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Proverbs 13:19-20, contrasting the wise and fools?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:19-20 contrasts 'wise' and 'fools,' using antithesis to highlight opposing outcomes.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of 'walking with the wise' from Proverbs 13:20?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:33 warns 'Bad company corrupts good morals,' echoing Proverbs 13:20's theme about companions influencing wisdom or destruction.

questions.question: Which Old Testament verse connects with Proverbs 13:22's teaching on leaving an inheritance?
questions.explanation: Psalm 37:25 speaks of a righteous man never being forsaken nor his children begging for bread, paralleling Proverbs 13:22 about inheritance.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Proverbs 13:19?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:18 comes just before 13:19 and discusses the consequences of refusing instruction or regarding reproof.

questions.question: Which Hebrew literary structure is evident in Proverbs 13:12 with the phrases 'Hope deferred maketh the heart sick' and 'when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life'?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:12 uses synonymous parallelism to contrast hope deferred with desire fulfilled, a hallmark of Hebrew poetry.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 13:6 employ typology in its depiction of righteousness and wickedness?
options: Righteousness as protection, wickedness as downfall
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness as protection, wickedness as downfall
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:6 typologically portrays righteousness as keeping the upright safe and wickedness causing sinners to fall, foreshadowing moral consequences.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:24 teaches that sparing discipline is an expression of love for one's son.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:24 says 'He that spareth his rod hateth his son,' indicating sparing discipline is not loving.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 13:25 states that the righteous eat to the satisfying of their soul.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:25 affirms 'The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul,' confirming the statement.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 13:3 teach about human sin and its consequences?
options: Guarding one’s speech preserves life, while careless words bring destruction
Human sin is forgiven by silence and discretion
Sinful words have no real impact on one’s spiritual state
Open confession of sin leads to immediate salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Guarding one’s speech preserves life, while careless words bring destruction
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:3 states, 'He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction,' teaching that controlling speech is crucial for preserving life, while careless words cause ruin.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does Proverbs 13:24 teach?
options: Loving discipline is necessary for a child’s growth and godly character
Sanctification is achieved without correction or rebuke
Children mature spiritually only through natural development
questions.correctAnswer: Loving discipline is necessary for a child’s growth and godly character
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:24 says, 'He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes,' teaching that loving discipline is essential for holiness and growth in the child.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of righteousness and wickedness does Proverbs 13:6 teach?
options: Righteousness preserves the upright, but wickedness leads to the sinner’s downfall
Righteousness and wickedness have no real effect on a person’s path
Wickedness sometimes benefits the sinner more than righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness preserves the upright, but wickedness leads to the sinner’s downfall
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:6 states, 'Righteousness keepeth him that is upright in the way: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner,' teaching the protective power of righteousness and the destructive nature of wickedness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 13:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:14 calls the law 'a fountain of life' and a guide to escape death’s snares, highlighting God’s wisdom in providing life-giving instruction.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 13:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:17 contrasts a wicked messenger with a faithful ambassador who brings health, illustrating God’s faithfulness in sending trustworthy messengers.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 13:20 connect to the broader biblical theme of community and holiness?
options: Walking with the wise fosters sanctification, while companionship with fools leads to destruction
Community has no impact on spiritual growth
Isolation is preferable to any form of companionship
Foolish companions can sometimes improve one’s wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Walking with the wise fosters sanctification, while companionship with fools leads to destruction
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:20 teaches that association influences spiritual condition, aligning with biblical themes like 1 Corinthians 15:33 about bad company corrupting good morals.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Proverbs 13:22 prepare for?
options: The doctrine of legacy and covenantal blessing through generations
The idea that wealth is ultimately meaningless
The rejection of inheritance as a spiritual concept
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of legacy and covenantal blessing through generations
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:22 discusses leaving an inheritance to children’s children, echoing covenant promises to Abraham about descendants and blessings (Genesis 17:7).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 13:1 and 13:18 teach about discipline and instruction?
options: Wise children accept correction and are honored, while those who reject rebuke face poverty and shame
Discipline is unnecessary for the wise
Instruction leads to shame and poverty
Rebuke is only for the wicked, not for the upright
questions.correctAnswer: Wise children accept correction and are honored, while those who reject rebuke face poverty and shame
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:1 teaches that a wise son hears instruction, and 13:18 says refusing instruction leads to poverty and shame, showing the importance of accepting discipline.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 13:9 and 13:21 teach about the destiny of the righteous and wicked?
options: The light of the righteous rejoices and good is repaid, while the wicked’s lamp is put out and evil pursues sinners
Both righteous and wicked share the same destiny
Wickedness is rewarded while righteousness is punished
The fate of the wicked is unknown
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the righteous rejoices and good is repaid, while the wicked’s lamp is put out and evil pursues sinners
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:9 and 13:21 contrast the prosperity and protection of the righteous with the destruction and pursuit of evil upon sinners.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 13:4 and 13:11 teach about diligence and wealth?
options: The diligent prosper through labor, while wealth gained hastily or by vanity diminishes
Wealth acquired quickly is the most stable
Diligence has no correlation with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The diligent prosper through labor, while wealth gained hastily or by vanity diminishes
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:4 praises diligence for satisfaction, and 13:11 warns that wealth gained by vanity lessens, teaching the doctrine of faithful labor.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Proverbs 13:12–13 promotes legalism by emphasizing fear and obedience. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Hope fulfilled brings life, and fearing God’s commandments leads to blessing, not legalistic bondage
It demands salvation by works alone
It encourages despair due to deferred hope
It teaches that fearing God is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Hope fulfilled brings life, and fearing God’s commandments leads to blessing, not legalistic bondage
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:12–13 contrasts the sickness caused by delayed hope with the life-giving fulfillment of desire and states that fearing the commandment results in reward, highlighting covenantal obedience, not legalism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 13:7 teach about the nature of true wealth?
options: External riches do not guarantee true wealth or security
Poverty is a sign of sinfulness
Material wealth is the ultimate measure of success
questions.correctAnswer: External riches do not guarantee true wealth or security
questions.explanation: Proverbs 13:7 states, 'There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches,' teaching that true wealth is not always visible materially.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Proverbs 13:6 through the preservation of the upright?
questions.explanation: The verse states righteousness keeps the upright in the way while wickedness destroys sinners, illustrating God’s justice in rewarding the righteous and punishing the wicked.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Proverbs 13:22 develop in connection with covenant theology?
options: God’s promise of blessing to future generations through faithful living
Rejection of all material blessings as sinful
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promise of blessing to future generations through faithful living
questions.explanation: The inheritance left to children’s children in Proverbs 13:22 reflects God’s covenantal promise to bless descendants, as seen in Abrahamic covenant passages.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 13:15 and 13:16 teach about wisdom and folly?
options: Good understanding leads to favor and prudent knowledge, while transgressors face a hard way and fools reveal their folly
Fools have greater insight than the wise
Wisdom and folly have equal outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: Good understanding leads to favor and prudent knowledge, while transgressors face a hard way and fools reveal their folly
questions.explanation: Verse 15 highlights favor given by good understanding, and 16 contrasts the prudent man’s knowledge with the fool’s exposed folly, teaching the consequences of wisdom versus folly.
